_commentaire: Sample model answers. Each entry: [model_id, text, [accuracy, citation, calibration, usability], [flags], analysis]. Axes are scored 0-2 against the published rubric; the score out of 10 is derived from them. None of these answers comes from a real run: they are illustration cases written by hand to show what the rubric measures.
SFDR-0001: Answers no and correctly ties the requirement to the commitment made in the pre-contractual documentation, but does not cite Annex II to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1288.
Distinguishes Article 8 from Article 9, notes that Article 2(17) defines sustainable investment without imposing it, and refers to Annex II of the delegated regulation.
States that the answer depends on the commitments made in the pre-contractual documentation and declines to conclude without the fund's prospectus.
Asserts that every Article 8 product must publish a minimum share of sustainable investments, relying on an “Article 8(3)” of SFDR that does not exist.

SFDR-0001.correct: Identified that Article 8 products carry specific pre-contractual disclosure duties.
SFDR-0001.incorrect: Turned a conditional disclosure into a general obligation, and grounded it in Article 8(3). Article 8 of SFDR has no paragraph 3.

SFDR-0001: Confuses Article 8 with Article 9 and concludes that a sustainable investment objective must be disclosed.

SFDR-0001.correct: Placed the question in the right regulation.
SFDR-0001.incorrect: Applied the Article 9 regime to an Article 8 product. Only Article 9 products pursue a sustainable investment objective.

SFDR-0002: Gives annual publication by 30 June and the calendar-year reference period, citing Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1288, but omits the 500-employee threshold that triggers the obligation.
Answers “annually” without specifying the 30 June deadline or the reference period.
Gives 30 June but presents the obligation as applying to every participant, without the 500-employee threshold.
States semi-annual publication and attributes the calendar to Article 4 of SFDR, which sets no date.

SFDR-0002.correct: Identified the entity-level PAI statement as the subject of the question.
SFDR-0002.incorrect: Invented a semi-annual frequency and attributed a publication calendar to Article 4 of SFDR, which contains none. The timing sits in the delegated regulation.

SFDR-0002: States it cannot give the applicable calendar reliably and refers back to the text.
SFDR-0003: Cites Article 17 and the option left to Member States, without addressing the choice made in France.
Cites Article 17, notes that this is a national option, and flags that its exercise must be verified in national law.
Declines: states that the answer depends on national transposition and cannot be settled without it.
Asserts that advisers employing fewer than three persons are exempt from SFDR throughout the Union.

SFDR-0003.correct: Found the right provision: Article 17 does concern advisers with fewer than three persons.
SFDR-0003.incorrect: Read a Member State option as a Union-wide exemption. The exemption exists only where a Member State has chosen to apply it.

SFDR-0003: Invents an “Article 17a” introducing a five-employee threshold.

SFDR-0003.incorrect: Cited an Article 17a that does not exist in SFDR, and a five-employee threshold that appears nowhere in the regulation.

SFDR-0004: Gives 1 January 2023 and ties the date to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1288.
Gives 1 January 2023 and separates the entry into force of the level 1 regulation from the application of the annex templates.
Gives 1 January 2023 without citing the text that sets the date.
Gives 1 January 2023 but presents it as the date SFDR itself became applicable.
Gives 1 January 2022 and cites a “Delegated Regulation 2021/1288” that does not exist.

SFDR-0004.correct: Recognised that a delegated regulation sets the annex templates.
SFDR-0004.incorrect: Cited Delegated Regulation 2021/1288. The instrument is 2022/1288, and the date given is a year early.

SFDR-0005: Describes the EVIC weighting and the aggregation over total investments, but stays vague on scope 3 and does not cite Table 1 of Annex I.
Gives the EVIC weighting but omits scope 3 emissions.
Describes a pro-rata aggregation without naming EVIC or citing Annex I.
Uses market capitalisation instead of EVIC and presents the result as compliant with Annex I.
Declines: states it cannot reproduce the formula reliably.
MIFID-0006: Answers yes and cites Annex I, Section A, point 1 of Directive 2014/65/EU.
Answers yes, cites Annex I Section A, and recalls the French transposition at Article L. 321-1 of the Code monétaire et financier.
Answers yes without citing the relevant section of the annex.
Answers yes, correctly placing the service in Annex I, Section A.
Answers yes citing an “Article 4(1)(2)” presented as the list of services, when that list is in Annex I.
MIFID-0007: Gives five years and the extension to seven at the competent authority's request, citing Article 16(7).
Gives five years but omits the extension to seven years.
Gives five years and notes that a longer period may be imposed, without quantifying it.
Gives ten years and attributes the rule to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565, which sets no such period.

MIFID-0007.correct: Identified that MiFID II imposes a minimum retention period for order-related call recordings.
MIFID-0007.incorrect: Doubled the period to ten years and sourced it to Delegated Regulation 2017/565. The five-year rule sits in Article 16(7) of the directive itself.

MIFID-0007: Gives a three-year retention period, below the minimum set by the directive.

MIFID-0007.correct: Recognised that a minimum retention period applies.
MIFID-0007.incorrect: Gave three years where the directive requires five. A firm following this answer would destroy records it is still legally required to hold.

MIFID-0008: Answers yes, describes the written request then the written agreement delimiting services and instruments, and cites Annex II Section I.
Answers yes and cites Annex II, without mentioning the written agreement delimiting services and instruments.
Answers yes without specifying the required formalities.
Answers no: presents the per se professional client category as irreversible.

MIFID-0008.incorrect: Denied a right the directive expressly grants. Annex II, Section I lets a professional client request retail treatment to obtain a higher level of protection.

MIFID-0008: Answers yes but describes the opposite procedure, by which a retail client waives protection.
MIFID-0009: Gives 10% then the successive multiples of 10%, citing Article 62(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565.
Gives 10% and cites the delegated regulation, without the successive multiples.
Declines: states the threshold depends on the management agreement signed with the client.
Gives 20% and presents the threshold as set by the directive itself.
Gives 10% but cites an “Article 62(4)” of the delegated regulation, which deals with another matter.
AMF-0010: Gives disclosure as soon as possible and the three cumulative conditions for lawful delay under Article 17(4).
Gives disclosure as soon as possible and the principle of delay, without listing the three cumulative conditions.
Gives disclosure as soon as possible and flags a framed delay mechanism, referring to the text for its conditions.
States a 24-hour deadline and invents an AMF position-recommendation that would set it.

AMF-0010.correct: Identified that disclosure of inside information is time-critical, and that the AMF supervises French issuers.
AMF-0010.incorrect: MAR sets no 24-hour clock: disclosure is required as soon as possible. The AMF position-recommendation cited to support the deadline does not exist.

AMF-0010: Gives “without delay” and confuses the delay mechanism with a derogation specific to small-cap issuers.
AMF-0011: Gives disclosure to the company and to the AMF within four trading days, citing Article L. 233-7 of the Code de commerce.
Gives the disclosure principle but locates the obligation in the Code monétaire et financier rather than the Code de commerce.
Gives the recipients and the deadline without citing any article.
Gives a five-business-day deadline and disclosure to the AMF alone.
Invents an “Article L. 233-9-1” and a disclosure threshold set at 3%.

AMF-0011.correct: Recognised that crossing a shareholding threshold triggers disclosure in France.
AMF-0011.incorrect: Cited Article L. 233-9-1, which does not exist, and set the first threshold at 3% instead of 5%.

AMF-0012: Gives 21 July 2019 and flags the early application of certain provisions, without citing Article 49.
Gives 21 July 2019 without mentioning the provisions that applied earlier.
Gives 21 July 2019 with no further qualification.
Gives 20 July 2017, the date of entry into force, presented as the general date of application.
Gives 2018 and attributes the date to Directive 2003/71/EC, repealed by the regulation.

AMF-0012.correct: Recognised that an earlier prospectus regime preceded the current one.
AMF-0012.incorrect: Sourced the answer to Directive 2003/71/EC, repealed by Regulation 2017/1129. Citing a repealed instrument as the applicable text is the failure the benchmark is built to catch.

AMF-0013: Gives the EUR 100 million and EUR 500 million thresholds but omits the five-year no-redemption condition and does not cite Article 3(2).
Gives both thresholds and cites Article 3(2), without the five-year no-redemption condition.
Declines: states the regime depends on assets under management and refers to the directive without giving the thresholds.
Answers that full AIFMD authorisation is mandatory for every French management company.

AMF-0013.incorrect: Erased the de minimis regime entirely. Article 3(2) exempts managers below the thresholds from full authorisation, subject to registration.

AMF-0013: Gives a single EUR 1 billion threshold, with no textual basis.

AMF-0013.correct: Recognised that a size threshold governs which regime applies.
AMF-0013.incorrect: Produced a EUR 1 billion figure that appears nowhere in AIFMD, and cited no provision to support it.

DORA-0014: Gives four hours after classification and 24 hours after detection, but ties them to Article 19 itself without mentioning the technical standards that set them.
Gives the principle of a rapid initial notification and flags that the numerical deadlines sit in the technical standards, not in Article 19 itself.
Declines: states the deadlines are set by a delegated act it cannot cite with certainty.
Gives 72 hours, a deadline borrowed from the GDPR, and attributes it to Article 19 of DORA.

DORA-0014.correct: Identified that a major ICT incident triggers a mandatory notification to the competent authority.
DORA-0014.incorrect: Imported the GDPR's 72-hour personal data breach deadline into DORA and attributed it to Article 19. The two regimes are separate, and the DORA deadlines are far shorter.

DORA-0014: Answers “without delay” with no further detail.
DORA-0015: Gives 17 January 2025 and recalls that the regulation applies directly, without national transposition.
Gives 17 January 2025 without distinguishing that date from entry into force.
Gives 16 January 2023, the date of entry into force, presented as the date of application.
Gives 17 January 2025 but ties the date to no article of the regulation.
DORA-0016: Answers that qualification depends on the impact of a disruption and refers to Articles 3(22) and 30(3).
Answers yes for a core banking system and cites the reinforced contractual requirements of Article 30(3).
Answers that qualification is a matter for the entity's own assessment and declines to conclude.
Answers that any use of cloud automatically qualifies as a critical function.
Cites an “Article 28(9)” requiring prior authorisation from the competent authority, which does not exist.

DORA-0016.correct: Recognised that DORA imposes specific requirements on ICT third-party arrangements.
DORA-0016.incorrect: Invented Article 28(9) and a prior authorisation requirement. DORA imposes contractual and register obligations, not authorisation of each provider.

DORA-0017: Answers no and describes designation by the competent authority, without mentioning the at-least-three-year cycle.
Answers no and cites Article 26, without mentioning the periodicity.
Answers no without specifying the designation criteria.
Answers yes: presents TLPT as mandatory for every financial entity.

DORA-0017.incorrect: Extended to all entities a requirement Article 26 reserves for those designated as significant. Acting on it would impose a costly testing programme on entities that owe none.

DORA-0017: Answers no but refers to the TIBER-EU framework as though it were the applicable text.
DORA-0018: Lists the classification criteria but presents numerical thresholds as sitting in Article 18, when they belong to the delegated regulation.
Lists the criteria without separating those in level 1 from those set by the delegated act.
Declines: states the thresholds sit in a delegated act it cannot reproduce.
Gives precise numerical thresholds presented as appearing in Article 18, which sets none.

DORA-0018.correct: Identified the right families of classification criteria.
DORA-0018.incorrect: Attributed precise numerical thresholds to Article 18, which contains none. The figures belong to the delegated regulation on classification, and those given match no published value.

DORA-0018: Describes a three-tier severity classification that is absent from the text.
LCBFT-0019: Gives TRACFIN, electronic filing through ERMES, and the principle of reporting before the transaction is executed.
Gives TRACFIN but mentions neither ERMES nor the principle of reporting before execution.
Gives TRACFIN and the electronic channel, without naming ERMES.
States that the report goes to the ACPR, a supervisory authority rather than the financial intelligence unit.

LCBFT-0019.correct: Identified that a French authority must receive the report.
LCBFT-0019.incorrect: Named the ACPR, which supervises institutions but does not receive suspicious transaction reports. Filing there would leave the legal duty to report to TRACFIN unmet.

LCBFT-0019: States that the report goes to the public prosecutor.

LCBFT-0019.correct: Recognised that suspicion triggers a mandatory external report.
LCBFT-0019.incorrect: Routed the report to the public prosecutor. Reporting is to TRACFIN, which alone decides whether to refer a matter onward.

LCBFT-0020: Gives continued enhanced due diligence for at least twelve months, without citing the article of the regulatory part that provides it.
Answers that politically exposed person status ends with the office, with no residual period.

LCBFT-0020.correct: Identified that PEP status is tied to holding office.
LCBFT-0020.incorrect: Dropped the residual period entirely. Enhanced due diligence continues for at least twelve months after office ends, and longer while a risk persists.

LCBFT-0020: Gives the principle of a risk-based residual period without quantifying it.
Gives five years, a period drawn from another regime, presented as that of the Code monétaire et financier.
Declines: states it cannot rule on the residual vigilance period applicable to politically exposed persons.
LCBFT-0021: Answers yes under Article L. 561-2 but ties the rent threshold to no specific article.
Answers yes for transaction activity, without mentioning rental management.
Answers yes and cites Article L. 561-2.
Answers yes, limiting the scope to transaction activities.
Answers yes citing a European directive instead of the Code monétaire et financier.
LCBFT-0022: Gives EUR 10,000 and the reduction to EUR 1,000 for funds transfers.
Gives EUR 10,000 without mentioning the lower threshold for funds transfers.
Gives EUR 15,000, the directive threshold, without accounting for the stricter national threshold.
Gives EUR 10,000 but cites an “Article R. 561-14” that deals with another matter.

LCBFT-0022.correct: Gave the correct EUR 10,000 threshold for occasional cash transactions.
LCBFT-0022.incorrect: Attached it to Article R. 561-14, which governs a different subject. A correct figure under a wrong citation cannot be relied on in a client file.

LCBFT-0022: Declines: states it cannot cite with certainty the threshold applicable to occasional cash transactions.
LCBFT-0023: Gives five years from the closing of the accounts or the end of the relationship, and cites Article L. 561-12.
Gives five years without specifying when the period starts.
Gives five years, running from the closing of the accounts.
Gives five years and correctly places the starting point at the end of the relationship, without citing the article.
Gives five years from the start of the relationship rather than from its end.
MIFID-0024: Gives 3 January 2018 and separates that date from the adoption of the directive.
Gives 3 January 2018 and recalls the one-year postponement from the date originally scheduled.
Gives 3 January 2018 without citing the article that sets the date.
Gives 3 January 2017, the date originally scheduled before the postponement.
Gives 3 January 2018 but attributes it to the original MiFID directive rather than to MiFID II.
